q: 老师昨天给我们留___三篇作业。
zh: 老师昨天给我们留了三篇作业。
py: lǎo shī zuó tiān gěi wǒ men liú le sān piān zuò yè
en: The teacher assigned us three pieces of homework yesterday.
why: One finished event with a counted object: 了 goes right after 留, before 三篇. 昨天 gives the time but cannot replace 了, so leaving it out fails; 着 describes a continuing state, not a finished act.

q: 我今天上午喝___两杯茶。
zh: 我今天上午喝了两杯茶。
py: wǒ jīn tiān shàng wǔ hē le liǎng bēi chá
en: I drank two cups of tea this morning.
why: The drinking is finished and the object is counted (两杯), so 了 sits right after 喝. Without it the sentence reads like a plan or a general statement, and 着 or 的 cannot mark a completed act.

q: 经理上午给我们开___一个会。
zh: 经理上午给我们开了一个会。
py: jīng lǐ shàng wǔ gěi wǒ men kāi le yí gè huì
en: The manager held a meeting for us this morning.
why: A single completed meeting with a counted noun takes 了 right after 开. 着 would make the meeting ongoing, and 的 turns 开 into a modifier of 一个会 instead of reporting the event.

q: 我们在图书馆复习___三个小时就回家了。
zh: 我们在图书馆复习了三个小时就回家了。
py: wǒ men zài tú shū guǎn fù xí le sān gè xiǎo shí jiù huí jiā le
en: We revised in the library for three hours and then went home.
why: A bounded stretch of time that ended (and was followed by going home) takes 了 after the verb. 过 is about having done something at some point in life, which does not fit a specific afternoon.

q: 小李上个星期写___五份报告。
zh: 小李上个星期写了五份报告。
py: xiǎo lǐ shàng gè xīng qī xiě le wǔ fèn bào gào
en: Last week Xiao Li wrote five reports.
why: 上个星期 is a closed past time and 五份报告 is a counted object, so 了 follows 写. A time word alone does not mark completion; 着 and 的 do not report a finished action.

q: 这次考试他考___八十分，老师很满意。
zh: 这次考试他考了八十分，老师很满意。
py: zhè cì kǎo shì tā kǎo le bā shí fēn lǎo shī hěn mǎn yì
en: He scored eighty on this exam and the teacher was pleased.
why: A result reached once, with a number, takes 了 right after the verb 考. 的 would need a noun to follow (考的成绩), and 着 gives an ongoing state; neither reports what happened.

q: 我上周三发___两封邮件给客户。
zh: 我上周三发了两封邮件给客户。
py: wǒ shàng zhōu sān fā le liǎng fēng yóu jiàn gěi kè hù
en: Last Wednesday I sent two emails to the client.
why: A completed action on a specific past day with a counted object needs 了 after 发. Without it, 两封邮件 reads like an instruction or plan, and 着 does not fit a one-off sending.

q: 为了准备明天的考试，我昨天晚上复习___整整四个小时的语法。
zh: 为了准备明天的考试，我昨天晚上复习了整整四个小时的语法。
py: wèi le zhǔn bèi míng tiān de kǎo shì wǒ zuó tiān wǎn shàng fù xí le zhěng zhěng sì gè xiǎo shí de yǔ fǎ
en: To prepare for tomorrow's exam, I spent a full four hours revising grammar last night.
why: The revising is over and bounded by 四个小时, so 了 goes right after 复习 even though the sentence mentions tomorrow. Leaving it out loses the sense of a finished event; 着 cannot take a time span.

q: 财务部上个月招___两个新同事，一个负责报销，一个负责工资。
zh: 财务部上个月招了两个新同事，一个负责报销，一个负责工资。
py: cái wù bù shàng gè yuè zhāo le liǎng gè xīn tóng shì yí gè fù zé bào xiāo yí gè fù zé gōng zī
en: Last month the finance department hired two new colleagues, one for expenses and one for payroll.
why: Hiring happened once last month and the object is counted, so 了 follows 招. 着 would mean the hiring is in progress, and 的 would make 招的两个新同事 a noun phrase with nothing to finish the sentence.

zh: 同学昨天借了两本词典。
py: tóng xué zuó tiān jiè le liǎng běn cí diǎn
en: My classmate borrowed two dictionaries yesterday.
why: With a counted object, 了 sits right after the verb 借 and before 两本词典. Leaving it for the end of the sentence is the tempting wrong order.

zh: 小李给客户发了两封邮件。
py: xiǎo lǐ gěi kè hù fā le liǎng fēng yóu jiàn
en: Xiao Li sent the client two emails.
why: The finished action takes 了 directly after 发, before the counted object 两封邮件. The 给客户 phrase stays before the verb.

zh: 他今天下午在会议室开了三个小时的会。
py: tā jīn tiān xià wǔ zài huì yì shì kāi le sān gè xiǎo shí de huì
en: This afternoon he spent three hours in a meeting in the meeting room.
why: A finished, timed event puts 了 right after 开, before 三个小时的会. Moving 了 to the end would change the sense to 'has been in a meeting for three hours so far'. The place phrase 在会议室 stays before the verb.

task: Say he drank two cups (add 两杯).
zh: 他喝了两杯咖啡。
py: tā hē le liǎng bēi kā fēi
en: He drank two cups of coffee.
why: Once the object is counted, 了 moves right after the verb and ends up before 两杯. The final 了 of the source sentence is no longer needed.

task: Say it happened: we waited for her for half an hour.
zh: 我们等了她半个小时。
py: wǒ men děng le tā bàn gè xiǎo shí
en: We waited for her for half an hour.
why: A finished stretch of waiting with a stated duration takes 了 right after the verb. The pronoun object 她 comes before the duration.

s: 老师昨天讲三个语法点。
s_py: lǎo shī zuó tiān jiǎng sān gè yǔ fǎ diǎn
zh: 老师昨天讲了三个语法点。
py: lǎo shī zuó tiān jiǎng le sān gè yǔ fǎ diǎn
en: The teacher covered three grammar points yesterday.
why: A finished event with a counted object needs 了 right after the verb. 昨天 shows the time but cannot replace 了; without it the sentence sounds like a plan or an unfinished clause.

s: 经理昨天去上海了。
s_py: jīng lǐ zuó tiān qù shàng hǎi le
zh: 经理昨天去上海了。
py: jīng lǐ zuó tiān qù shàng hǎi le
en: The manager went to Shanghai yesterday.
why: This is correct: with a plain place object and no number, a simple report of a finished trip puts 了 at the end of the sentence. It is not wrong to leave 了 off the verb here.

s: 小王写了那份报告。
s_py: xiǎo wáng xiě le nà fèn bào gào
zh: 小王写了那份报告。
py: xiǎo wáng xiě le nà fèn bào gào
en: Xiao Wang wrote that report.
why: This is correct: 那份报告 is a specific object, so 了 may follow the verb directly. Learners often think verb + 了 needs a number, but a specific object works just as well.

s: 上个星期公司招两个新同事，他们都是学经济的。
s_py: shàng gè xīng qī gōng sī zhāo liǎng gè xīn tóng shì tā men dōu shì xué jīng jì de
zh: 上个星期公司招了两个新同事，他们都是学经济的。
py: shàng gè xīng qī gōng sī zhāo le liǎng gè xīn tóng shì tā men dōu shì xué jīng jì de
en: Last week the company hired two new colleagues, both of whom studied economics.
why: The hiring is a single finished event with a counted object, so 招 needs 了. 上个星期 is only a time word; without 了 the clause sounds like a plan, not a fact.

q: 天黑___，我们回家吧。
zh: 天黑了，我们回家吧。
py: tiān hēi le wǒ men huí jiā ba
en: It's dark now, let's go home.
why: Sentence-final 了 reports a new situation: it was light, now it is dark. 过 and 着 do not mark a change, and 的 would make 天黑的 a noun-like phrase.

q: 刚才不饿，现在我饿___。
zh: 刚才不饿，现在我饿了。
py: gāng cái bù è xiàn zài wǒ è le
en: I wasn't hungry a moment ago, but now I am.
why: The cue says a change happened (not hungry before, hungry now), so the sentence ends with 了. 饿 with nothing after it describes a state with no hint of change, which contradicts 刚才不饿.

q: 我女儿已经八岁___，该上学了。
zh: 我女儿已经八岁了，该上学了。
py: wǒ nǚ ér yǐ jīng bā suì le gāi shàng xué le
en: My daughter is already eight, so it is time for her to start school.
why: An age reached now is a new situation, and 已经 asks for 了 at the end: 八岁了. 的 and 着 cannot close an age expression.

q: 小王学了三个月，现在会用这个软件___。
zh: 小王学了三个月，现在会用这个软件了。
py: xiǎo wáng xué le sān gè yuè xiàn zài huì yòng zhè ge ruǎn jiàn le
en: Xiao Wang has studied for three months, and now he can use this software.
why: 会 + verb + 了 says he has newly acquired the skill. 过 would mean he has used it before, and 着 or 的 does not close the sentence.

q: 快考试___，同学们都在复习。
zh: 快考试了，同学们都在复习。
py: kuài kǎo shì le tóng xué men dōu zài fù xí
en: The exam is about to start and everyone is revising.
why: 快 … 了 frames an event that is about to happen as a change on its way. 过 and 着 do not fit 快, and 的 is not a closing particle here.

q: 现在已经十一点___，你该睡觉了。
zh: 现在已经十一点了，你该睡觉了。
py: xiàn zài yǐ jīng shí yī diǎn le nǐ gāi shuì jiào le
en: It's already eleven o'clock, you should go to bed.
why: A clock time reached now, with 已经, is a changed situation and takes final 了. 的 and 着 do not close a time expression, and 过 would shift the meaning to 'has passed eleven in the past'.

q: 会议下个月就要开始___，我们得赶紧把材料准备好。
zh: 会议下个月就要开始了，我们得赶紧把材料准备好。
py: huì yì xià gè yuè jiù yào kāi shǐ le wǒ men dé gǎn jǐn bǎ cái liào zhǔn bèi hǎo
en: The conference starts next month, so we have to get the materials ready quickly.
why: 就要 … 了 marks something that is about to happen. 着 and 过 cannot follow 开始 in this pattern, and 的 would turn 就要开始 into a modifier without a closing sentence.

q: 天气渐渐冷___，办公室里也开始开暖气了。
zh: 天气渐渐冷了，办公室里也开始开暖气了。
py: tiān qì jiàn jiàn lěng le bàn gōng shì lǐ yě kāi shǐ kāi nuǎn qì le
en: The weather has gradually turned cold and the office has started to turn on the heating.
why: The 渐渐 shows a change in progress, so the adjective 冷 takes final 了 for 'has become cold'. 着 would mean it stays cold, and 过 would mean it was cold at some earlier point.

zh: 考试快要开始了。
py: kǎo shì kuài yào kāi shǐ le
en: The exam is about to start.
why: 快要 … 了 wraps around the verb: it frames the coming event as a change under way. 了 must close the sentence, not follow 快要.

zh: 他现在会说汉语了。
py: tā xiàn zài huì shuō hàn yǔ le
en: He can speak Chinese now.
why: 现在 and 了 together say this is a new ability: 了 goes at the end after the whole verb phrase. Without it the sentence is a plain statement about ability.

task: Say he can drive now (he has just learned).
zh: 他会开车了。
py: tā huì kāi chē le
en: He can drive now.
why: Adding sentence-final 了 turns the plain ability statement into a new situation: he did not use to be able to drive, but now he can.

s: 火车快了要开。
s_py: huǒ chē kuài le yào kāi
zh: 火车快要开了。
py: huǒ chē kuài yào kāi le
en: The train is about to leave.
why: 快要 is a unit and 了 closes the clause after the verb: 快要开了. Splitting 快 and 要 with 了 is not possible.

s: 我儿子五岁了。
s_py: wǒ ér zi wǔ suì le
zh: 我儿子五岁了。
py: wǒ ér zi wǔ suì le
en: My son is five now.
why: This is correct: an age takes sentence-final 了 when it has just been reached. It looks odd to learners because 了 follows a number, not a verb.

s: 我们的新同事已经会用这个系统了。
s_py: wǒ men de xīn tóng shì yǐ jīng huì yòng zhè ge xì tǒng le
zh: 我们的新同事已经会用这个系统了。
py: wǒ men de xīn tóng shì yǐ jīng huì yòng zhè ge xì tǒng le
en: Our new colleague can already use this system.
why: This is correct: 已经 + 会 + verb phrase + 了 says the skill is now in place. The 了 at the end marks the change, not a completed action.

q: 我已经学___两年中文___。
zh: 我已经学了两年中文了。
py: wǒ yǐ jīng xué le liǎng nián zhōng wén le
en: I've been studying Chinese for two years now.
why: Time so far and still going: 了 after the verb for the amount, a second 了 at the end for 'up to now'. With 已经, one 了 alone reads as a closed stretch, and with no 了 it is not marked as done at all.

q: 他到现在已经喝___三杯咖啡___。
zh: 他到现在已经喝了三杯咖啡了。
py: tā dào xiàn zài yǐ jīng hē le sān bēi kā fēi le
en: So far he has already drunk three cups of coffee.
why: 到现在 and 已经 make this a count so far: 了 after 喝 for the amount and 了 at the end for 'up to now'. With one 了 the three cups sound finished and closed; with none, nothing marks the count as done.

q: 我们等___一个小时___，经理还没来。
zh: 我们等了一个小时了，经理还没来。
py: wǒ men děng le yí gè xiǎo shí le jīng lǐ hái méi lái
en: We've been waiting for an hour and the manager still hasn't come.
why: 还没来 shows the waiting is still going on: 了 after the verb for the amount, 了 at the end for 'so far'. 着 cannot take a time span, and with no 了 the hour is not marked as done at all.

q: 我去年在上海住___三个月___。
zh: 我去年在上海住了三个月。
py: wǒ qù nián zài shàng hǎi zhù le sān gè yuè
en: Last year I lived in Shanghai for three months.
why: 去年 closes the time frame: the three months are over, so one 了 after the verb is enough. A second final 了 would claim the stay still counts up to now, which clashes with 去年.

q: 小李以前在这家公司工作___五年___，后来去了别的公司。
zh: 小李以前在这家公司工作了五年，后来去了别的公司。
py: xiǎo lǐ yǐ qián zài zhè jiā gōng sī gōng zuò le wǔ nián hòu lái qù le bié de gōng sī
en: Xiao Li used to work at this company for five years before moving to another one.
why: 后来去了别的公司 shows the five years ended in the past, so only the verb 了 is used. The final 了 would say he is still there, which contradicts the sentence.

q: 我已经在这个办公室坐___整整八个小时___，腰都疼了。
zh: 我已经在这个办公室坐了整整八个小时了，腰都疼了。
py: wǒ yǐ jīng zài zhè ge bàn gōng shì zuò le zhěng zhěng bā gè xiǎo shí le yāo dōu téng le
en: I've been sitting in this office for a full eight hours already, and my back is sore.
why: 已经 and the ongoing sitting give 'so far': 了 after 坐 and 了 at the end after 小时. 着 cannot take a time span, and with no 了 nothing marks the eight hours as counted up to now.

zh: 他已经工作了三年了。
py: tā yǐ jīng gōng zuò le sān nián le
en: He has already been working for three years.
why: 已经 asks for two 了: one after 工作 for the length of time and one at the end for 'so far'. A single 了 would turn it into a closed stretch of time.

src_py: wǒ xué le liǎng nián yīng yǔ
task: Say you have been studying for two years and still are.
zh: 我学了两年英语了。
py: wǒ xué le liǎng nián yīng yǔ le
en: I've been studying English for two years now.
why: Adding a second 了 at the end turns the closed amount into 'so far, still going'. The first 了 stays right after the verb.

s: 他已经喝了三杯咖啡了。
s_py: tā yǐ jīng hē le sān bēi kā fēi le
zh: 他已经喝了三杯咖啡了。
py: tā yǐ jīng hē le sān bēi kā fēi le
en: He has already had three cups of coffee.
why: This is correct: 已经 plus a counted amount takes both 了, one after the verb and one at the end. It looks like a repeated 了 error but is the standard 'so far' pattern.

s: 她小时候在上海住了三年了，后来搬到了北京。
s_py: tā xiǎo shí hou zài shàng hǎi zhù le sān nián le hòu lái bān dào le běi jīng
zh: 她小时候在上海住了三年，后来搬到了北京。
py: tā xiǎo shí hou zài shàng hǎi zhù le sān nián hòu lái bān dào le běi jīng
en: When she was little she lived in Shanghai for three years, and later moved to Beijing.
why: 后来搬到了北京 shows the three years are over, so only one 了 is used. The final 了 would claim she still counts those years up to now, which contradicts moving away.

q: 我吃___饭就去上课。
zh: 我吃了饭就去上课。
py: wǒ chī le fàn jiù qù shàng kè
en: I'll go to class as soon as I've eaten.
why: In 'after A, then B', 了 follows the first verb, before its object. It marks that A is done, and 着 (still eating) or 的 does not give that sense.

q: 下___课，我们就去吃饭。
zh: 下了课，我们就去吃饭。
py: xià le kè wǒ men jiù qù chī fàn
en: After class we'll go and eat.
why: 下了课 means 'once class is over', and 就 links it to the next step. 着 cannot attach to 下 here, and 过 would mean a past experience.

q: 你写___作业再玩手机。
zh: 你写了作业再玩手机。
py: nǐ xiě le zuò yè zài wán shǒu jī
en: Finish your homework before you play with your phone.
why: 写了作业再玩手机 says do the second thing once the first is finished. 着 would mean doing both at once, and 在 is not a particle that goes after the verb.

q: 他昨天下___班就回家了。
zh: 他昨天下了班就回家了。
py: tā zuó tiān xià le bān jiù huí jiā le
en: Yesterday he went home as soon as he finished work.
why: In 下了班就 ... the 了 after 下 shows work was over before he left. 着 and 过 do not fit, and 的 would turn 下班 into a modifier.

q: 明天开___会，我们再讨论这个问题。
zh: 明天开了会，我们再讨论这个问题。
py: míng tiān kāi le huì wǒ men zài tǎo lùn zhè ge wèn tí
en: After tomorrow's meeting we'll discuss this problem.
why: Even in the future, 了 after the first verb says once that step is finished, then 再 brings the next. 着 would mean discussing during the meeting, and 在 does not follow a verb.

q: 等我吃___午饭，看___那份文件，就给你回电话。
zh: 等我吃了午饭，看了那份文件，就给你回电话。
py: děng wǒ chī le wǔ fàn kàn le nà fèn wén jiàn jiù gěi nǐ huí diàn huà
en: After I've had lunch and looked at that document, I'll call you back.
why: Both steps happen before 就, so each first verb takes 了: 吃了午饭 and 看了那份文件. 着 would mean the steps are happening at once, which cannot lead into 就.

zh: 我吃了两个面包就去上课。
py: wǒ chī le liǎng gè miàn bāo jiù qù shàng kè
en: I'll go to class as soon as I've eaten two rolls.
why: 了 sits right after 吃, before the counted object 两个面包, and 就 then links the next step. 了 cannot go after 面包 because it marks the first step as done.

zh: 你写了报告再回家。
py: nǐ xiě le bào gào zài huí jiā
en: Finish the report before you go home.
why: Verb 了 + object, then 再 + the next action: 写了报告再回家. 再 means only then, so the order of the two steps cannot be reversed.

zh: 他昨天开了一个会就去机场了。
py: tā zuó tiān kāi le yí gè huì jiù qù jī chǎng le
en: Yesterday he went to the airport right after a meeting.
why: In a past sequence, 了 follows 开 (before the counted 一个会) and a second 了 closes the sentence. 昨天 may precede or follow the subject.

src: 我吃完这碗面，然后去上班。
src_py: wǒ chī wán zhè wǎn miàn rán hòu qù shàng bān
task: Combine into one sentence with 就 (once I've eaten, I go).
zh: 我吃了这碗面就去上班。
py: wǒ chī le zhè wǎn miàn jiù qù shàng bān
en: I'll go to work as soon as I've eaten this bowl of noodles.
why: 'After A, then B' with 就 uses verb + 了 + object for the first step, and 就 joins the second. The pair 吃完 + 然后 becomes one sentence.

s: 你洗手再吃了饭。
s_py: nǐ xǐ shǒu zài chī le fàn
zh: 你洗了手再吃饭。
py: nǐ xǐ le shǒu zài chī fàn
en: Wash your hands before you eat.
why: 了 belongs after the first step (洗了手), because it marks that step as done before 再. Putting it after 吃 would make eating the completed step instead.

s: 明天我们开了会再决定要不要买。
s_py: míng tiān wǒ men kāi le huì zài jué dìng yào bù yào mǎi
zh: 明天我们开了会再决定要不要买。
py: míng tiān wǒ men kāi le huì zài jué dìng yào bù yào mǎi
en: Tomorrow we'll hold the meeting first and then decide whether to buy it.
why: This is correct: 了 after the first verb in a 再 sequence is used for the future too. It is a trap because 明天 makes learners reject 了.

q: 我每天早上六点起___床。
zh: 我每天早上六点起床。
py: wǒ měi tiān zǎo shàng liù diǎn qǐ chuáng
en: I get up at six every morning.
why: 每天 makes this a routine, and routines take no 了. 了 would mean one finished event of getting up, which clashes with 每天.

q: 他常常在图书馆看___书。
zh: 他常常在图书馆看书。
py: tā cháng cháng zài tú shū guǎn kàn shū
en: He often reads in the library.
why: 常常 marks a repeated habit, so there is no 了. Adding 了 turns it into one completed reading event, which does not fit 常常.

q: 上大学的时候，我每天都在食堂吃___早饭。
zh: 上大学的时候，我每天都在食堂吃早饭。
py: shàng dà xué de shí hòu wǒ měi tiān dōu zài shí táng chī zǎo fàn
en: When I was at university I ate breakfast in the canteen every day.
why: The sentence is about the past, but 每天都 makes it a habit. Past habits take no 了 in Chinese, even though English uses the past tense.

q: 以前老师总是让我们背___课文。
zh: 以前老师总是让我们背课文。
py: yǐ qián lǎo shī zǒng shì ràng wǒ men bèi kè wén
en: The teacher always used to make us memorise the texts.
why: 总是 describes a repeated pattern in the past, so there is no 了. A 了 after 背 would turn it into a single completed act.

q: 刚上班的时候，经理一般都会在周一早上开___会，讨论这个星期的安排。
zh: 刚上班的时候，经理一般都会在周一早上开会，讨论这个星期的安排。
py: gāng shàng bān de shí hòu jīng lǐ yì bān dū huì zài zhōu yī zǎo shàng kāi huì tǎo lùn zhè ge xīng qī de ān pái
en: When I first started working, the manager usually held a meeting on Monday mornings to discuss the week's plans.
why: 一般都会 marks a regular routine, so 开会 stays bare. 了 would claim one completed meeting, which clashes with 一般 and with the habit of weekly meetings.

src_py: wǒ zuó tiān qù tú shū guǎn le
task: Say you go to the library every day (a habit).
zh: 我每天去图书馆。
py: wǒ měi tiān qù tú shū guǎn
en: I go to the library every day.
why: 每天 turns the sentence into a routine, and routines carry no 了. The 了 of the single-event source must be dropped.

s: 他以前每天骑了自行车去学校。
s_py: tā yǐ qián měi tiān qí le zì xíng chē qù xué xiào
zh: 他以前每天骑自行车去学校。
py: tā yǐ qián měi tiān qí zì xíng chē qù xué xiào
en: He used to cycle to school every day.
why: 每天 marks a habit, so 骑 takes no 了 even though it is in the past. 了 would suggest one finished ride, which clashes with 每天.

s: 以前我们每个星期都要考试，所以大家都很紧张。
s_py: yǐ qián wǒ men měi gè xīng qī dōu yào kǎo shì suǒ yǐ dà jiā dōu hěn jǐn zhāng
zh: 以前我们每个星期都要考试，所以大家都很紧张。
py: yǐ qián wǒ men měi gè xīng qī dōu yào kǎo shì suǒ yǐ dà jiā dōu hěn jǐn zhāng
en: In the old days we had a test every week, so everyone was tense.
why: This is correct: a past habit and a past state both take no 了, and 以前 carries the past. Learners often want a 了 after 考试 because of English past tense.

q: 同学们都没做___作业。
zh: 同学们都没做作业。
py: tóng xué men dōu méi zuò zuò yè
en: None of the students did the homework.
why: 没 already says the action did not happen, so 了 cannot be added. 没做了作业 would mix a negation with a completed-action marker.

q: 他还没吃___午饭。
zh: 他还没吃午饭。
py: tā hái méi chī wǔ fàn
en: He hasn't eaten lunch yet.
why: 还没 + verb says it has not happened yet, so 了 is never added. 了 marks that something is completed and contradicts 还没.

q: 我昨天___去上课。
zh: 我昨天没去上课。
py: wǒ zuó tiān méi qù shàng kè
en: I didn't go to class yesterday.
why: To say an action did not happen, use 没 + verb. 不 + verb is for habits or refusals, not for 'did not' in the past, and 别 is a command.

q: 作业太难了，我们小组到现在还___做完。
zh: 作业太难了，我们小组到现在还没做完。
py: zuò yè tài nán le wǒ men xiǎo zǔ dào xiàn zài hái méi zuò wán
en: The homework is too hard; our group still hasn't finished it.
why: 还 + 没 + verb says an action has not been completed yet. 不做完 would mean a refusal to finish, and 别 is a command.

q: 虽然老师提醒了好几次，可是他还是没有按时交___作业。
zh: 虽然老师提醒了好几次，可是他还是没有按时交作业。
py: suī rán lǎo shī tí xǐng le hǎo jǐ cì kě shì tā hái shì méi yǒu àn shí jiāo zuò yè
en: Although the teacher reminded him several times, he still didn't hand in his homework on time.
why: 没有 already negates the event, so 交作业 takes no 了. Learners are tempted to add 了 because the sentence is about the past and the earlier clause has 了.

zh: 他昨天没有来上班。
py: tā zuó tiān méi yǒu lái shàng bān
en: He didn't come to work yesterday.
why: 没有 sits directly before the verb and nothing else is needed: no 了. The time word 昨天 can come before or after the subject.

zh: 我没去学校。
py: wǒ méi qù xué xiào
en: I didn't go to school.
why: Negating a completed action replaces verb + 了 with 没 + verb. 了 must be deleted, and 不 is not used for 'did not'.

src: 他昨天给经理发了邮件。
src_py: tā zuó tiān gěi jīng lǐ fà le yóu jiàn
zh: 他昨天没给经理发邮件。
py: tā zuó tiān méi gěi jīng lǐ fà yóu jiàn
en: He didn't send the manager an email yesterday.
why: The negative of a finished action is 没 + verb with no 了. 没 goes before the whole verb phrase that follows the subject and time word.

s: 我昨天没买了三本书。
s_py: wǒ zuó tiān méi mǎi le sān běn shū
zh: 我昨天没买三本书。
py: wǒ zuó tiān méi mǎi sān běn shū
en: I didn't buy three books yesterday.
why: 没 and verb + 了 cannot appear together: 没 already says it did not happen. 没买了 is a classic error and a native speaker hears it as plainly wrong.

s: 他还没来上班，可能路上堵车了。
s_py: tā hái méi lái shàng bān kě néng lù shàng dǔ chē le
zh: 他还没来上班，可能路上堵车了。
py: tā hái méi lái shàng bān kě néng lù shàng dǔ chē le
en: He hasn't come to work yet; maybe he's stuck in traffic.
why: This is correct: 还没来上班 has no 了, while the second clause 堵车了 is a separate new situation with its own final 了. They do not clash.

q: 昨天天气很冷___，我们没去操场。
zh: 昨天天气很冷，我们没去操场。
py: zuó tiān tiān qì hěn lěng wǒ men méi qù cāo chǎng
en: It was cold yesterday, so we didn't go to the sports field.
why: This describes how things were, not an event, and 昨天 shows it is past. 了 would suggest it just turned cold, and 很 + adjective takes none.

q: 他以前是___我的同学。
zh: 他以前是我的同学。
py: tā yǐ qián shì wǒ de tóng xué
en: He used to be my classmate.
why: 是 is not an action that can be completed, so 是了 never means 'was'. 以前 carries the past, and the sentence needs nothing more.

q: 我觉得___这次考试很难。
zh: 我觉得这次考试很难。
py: wǒ jué de zhè cì kǎo shì hěn nán
en: I thought this exam was difficult.
why: 觉得 is a mental state, not a finished action, so it takes no 了 even when the opinion is about the past. 了 would suggest the thought just changed.

q: 小时候我很喜欢___语文课，不太喜欢数学课。
zh: 小时候我很喜欢语文课，不太喜欢数学课。
py: xiǎo shí hòu wǒ hěn xǐ huān yǔ wén kè bù tài xǐ huān shù xué kè
en: As a child I really liked Chinese class but didn't care much for maths.
why: 喜欢 is a state of liking, so no 了 even for something in the past. The time phrase 小时候 already places it in the past.

q: 当时我不知道___他是新来的经理，所以没有跟他打招呼。
zh: 当时我不知道他是新来的经理，所以没有跟他打招呼。
py: dāng shí wǒ bù zhī dào tā shì xīn lái de jīng lǐ suǒ yǐ méi yǒu gēn tā dǎ zhāo hū
en: At the time I didn't know he was the new manager, so I didn't greet him.
why: 知道 here is a past state of not knowing, and 不 + 知道 takes no 了. 当时 sets the time. The change-of-state 我知道了 is a different use.

zh: 昨天办公室里很热。
py: zuó tiān bàn gōng shì lǐ hěn rè
en: It was hot in the office yesterday.
why: A past state with 很 + adjective takes no 了: 昨天 supplies the past. The tiles must not include 了.

s: 他去年是了我们的数学老师。
s_py: tā qù nián shì le wǒ men de shù xué lǎo shī
zh: 他去年是我们的数学老师。
py: tā qù nián shì wǒ men de shù xué lǎo shī
en: Last year he was our maths teacher.
why: 是 never takes 了 to mean 'was'; it describes a state, and 去年 already says it was in the past. 是了 is a plain error.

s: 昨天晚上办公室里一个人都没有，只有我在加班。
s_py: zuó tiān wǎn shàng bàn gōng shì lǐ yí gè rén dōu méi yǒu zhǐ yǒu wǒ zài jiā bān
zh: 昨天晚上办公室里一个人都没有，只有我在加班。
py: zuó tiān wǎn shàng bàn gōng shì lǐ yí gè rén dōu méi yǒu zhǐ yǒu wǒ zài jiā bān
en: Last night there was nobody in the office; only I was working overtime.
why: This is correct: 没有 describes a past state, and 在加班 is an action in progress. Neither needs 了, even though learners want one for 'was nobody'.

q: 这本书太贵___，我不买。
zh: 这本书太贵了，我不买。
py: zhè běn shū tài guì le wǒ bù mǎi
en: This book is too expensive, I'm not buying it.
why: 太 + adjective as a remark is closed by 了: 太贵了. 的 and 着 cannot close it, and 吧 would turn it into a suggestion.

q: 你的汉语太好___！
zh: 你的汉语太好了！
py: nǐ de hàn yǔ tài hǎo le
en: Your Chinese is so good!
why: The exclamatory 太好了 is closed by 了. 的 would need a noun after it, and 吗 or 吧 would turn the compliment into a question or a guess.

q: 这次考试太难___，很多同学都没及格。
zh: 这次考试太难了，很多同学都没及格。
py: zhè cì kǎo shì tài nán le hěn duō tóng xué dōu méi jí gé
en: This exam was too hard, and many students failed.
why: 太 + adjective needs 了 to close the remark: 太难了. 着 does not close an adjective, and 的 would mean the adjective is modifying a noun.

q: 这个星期作业太多___，我周末也得写。
zh: 这个星期作业太多了，我周末也得写。
py: zhè ge xīng qī zuò yè tài duō le wǒ zhōu mò yě dé xiě
en: There is too much homework this week, so I have to write it over the weekend too.
why: The complaint 太多了 ends in 了. 的 would need a noun (太多的作业), and 着 or 过 cannot close an adjective.

q: 老板要我们今天就交方案，时间太紧___，恐怕来不及。
zh: 老板要我们今天就交方案，时间太紧了，恐怕来不及。
py: lǎo bǎn yào wǒ men jīn tiān jiù jiāo fāng àn shí jiān tài jǐn le kǒng pà lái bù jí
en: The boss wants the proposal today, and time is too tight, so I'm afraid we won't make it.
why: A comment of the 太 + adjective type is closed by 了: 太紧了. 着 and 过 do not close an adjective, and 的 would require a noun to follow.

zh: 这个字太难了。
py: zhè ge zì tài nán le
en: This character is too difficult.
why: 太 comes before the adjective and 了 closes the remark: 太难了. The 了 cannot be moved in front of 难.

src_py: zhè jiàn shì hěn zhòng yào
task: Say 'this matter is so important!' with 太.
zh: 这件事太重要了。
py: zhè jiàn shì tài zhòng yào le
en: This matter is so important!
why: A 太 remark replaces 很 and needs 了 at the end: 太重要了. 很 and 太 are not used together here.

s: 这个房间太了小。
s_py: zhè ge fáng jiān tài le xiǎo
zh: 这个房间太小了。
py: zhè ge fáng jiān tài xiǎo le
en: This room is too small.
why: 了 closes the 太 + adjective remark, so it goes after the adjective: 太小了. It cannot be placed between 太 and 小.

q: 我现在不喝咖啡___。
zh: 我现在不喝咖啡了。
py: wǒ xiàn zài bù hē kā fēi le
en: I don't drink coffee any more.
why: 'Not any more' is a change of situation, so 不 + verb takes 了 at the end. Without 了 it is a plain 'I don't drink coffee', with no sense of change.

q: 太晚了，我不去___。
zh: 太晚了，我不去了。
py: tài wǎn le wǒ bù qù le
en: It's too late, I'm not going after all.
why: A changed decision is 不 + verb + 了. 过 would refer to a past experience, 着 does not follow 去 here, and 吗 would turn it into a question.

q: 他已经不在这家公司工作___。
zh: 他已经不在这家公司工作了。
py: tā yǐ jīng bù zài zhè jiā gōng sī gōng zuò le
en: He doesn't work at this company any more.
why: 已经不 … 了 is 'no longer': the 了 at the end marks the change. 着 and 过 do not close this pattern, and 的 would need a noun.

q: 办公室里的咖啡喝完了，现在一点咖啡都没有___。
zh: 办公室里的咖啡喝完了，现在一点咖啡都没有了。
py: bàn gōng shì lǐ de kā fēi hē wán le xiàn zài yì diǎn kā fēi dōu méi yǒu le
en: The coffee in the office is finished, and now there's none left.
why: 没有 + noun + 了 says 'none left' as a new situation. 着 and 过 do not close this pattern, and 的 would require a noun after it.

q: 本来想去参加那个会，可是下雨了，所以我不想去___。
zh: 本来想去参加那个会，可是下雨了，所以我不想去了。
py: běn lái xiǎng qù cān jiā nà ge huì kě shì xià yǔ le suǒ yǐ wǒ bù xiǎng qù le
en: I originally wanted to go to that meeting, but it rained, so now I don't want to go.
why: A changed attitude is 不 + 想 + verb + 了. The earlier plan makes this a change of mind, which 着 and 过 cannot express.

q: 听说那个培训班要考试，我不报名___，还是自己在家学吧。
zh: 听说那个培训班要考试，我不报名了，还是自己在家学吧。
py: tīng shuō nà ge péi xùn bān yào kǎo shì wǒ bù bào míng le hái shì zì jǐ zài jiā xué ba
en: I heard that training course has an exam, so I won't sign up after all and will study at home.
why: 不报名了 expresses a changed decision after new information. 过 and 着 do not close the sentence, and 的 would require a noun. 还是 confirms the change of plan.

zh: 我不喝咖啡了。
py: wǒ bù hē kā fēi le
en: I don't drink coffee any more.
why: 不 + verb + 了 is the pattern for 'not any more': the 了 closes the sentence. Putting 了 after 喝 would turn it into a completed action.

zh: 下雨了我们不出去了。
py: xià yǔ le wǒ men bù chū qù le
en: It's raining, so we're not going out after all.
why: The 了 closes the sentence after 不出去 as a changed plan. The reason 下雨了 may come first or last, but 不出去了 stays as a unit.

zh: 因为天气不好我们不去旅行了。
py: yīn wèi tiān qì bù hǎo wǒ men bù qù lǚ xíng le
en: Because the weather is bad, we're not going on the trip after all.
why: 不 + verb + 了 shows the plan has changed. The 了 stays at the end, and 因为 can come before or after the subject.

src_py: wǒ xiǎng qù nà jiā gōng sī shàng bān
task: Say you changed your mind: you don't want to any more.
zh: 我不想去那家公司上班了。
py: wǒ bù xiǎng qù nà jiā gōng sī shàng bān le
en: I don't want to work at that company any more.
why: Changing 想 to 不想 plus a final 了 gives 'no longer want'. 了 must go at the end.

s: 我不吃了肉。
s_py: wǒ bù chī le ròu
zh: 我不吃肉了。
py: wǒ bù chī ròu le
en: I don't eat meat any more.
why: 'Not any more' puts 了 at the end of the whole clause: 不吃肉了. 了 cannot follow the verb directly here.

s: 太累了，我今天不加班了。
s_py: tài lèi le wǒ jīn tiān bù jiā bān le
zh: 太累了，我今天不加班了。
py: tài lèi le wǒ jīn tiān bù jiā bān le
en: I'm too tired, I'm not working overtime today after all.
why: This is correct: the second 了 closes 不加班 as a changed decision, and the first closes the 太 remark. Learners suspect two 了 are too many, but these are two different uses.
